literal_meaning: A single slice of baked cake
real_meaning: Something that is very easy to accomplish
example: Don't worry about the grammar quiz; it will be a piece of cake!

literal_meaning: Fracture or snap a leg bone
real_meaning: Good luck (traditionally used before a performance)
example: You are going to do great in the play tonight—break a leg!

literal_meaning: Chomp down on a lead bullet
real_meaning: To face a difficult situation with courage and get it over with
example: I decided to bite the bullet and go to the dentist for my checkup.

literal_meaning: Give the day a title or name
real_meaning: To stop working on something for the rest of the day
example: We have been studying for six hours, so let's call it a day.

literal_meaning: Tip over a bowl of beans onto the floor
real_meaning: To reveal a secret unexpectedly or prematurely
example: We were planning a surprise party, but Mark spilled the beans.

literal_meaning: Keep an oil lamp burning late at night
real_meaning: To stay up late studying or working
example: She had to burn the midnight oil to prepare for her final exams.

idiom: Hit the nail on the head
literal_meaning: Strike a metal nail precisely on its flat head
real_meaning: To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem
example: Her assessment of the market trend hit the nail on the head.

literal_meaning: Positioned physically underneath atmospheric weather
real_meaning: Slightly unwell, sick, or exhausted
example: I won't be coming to soccer practice today because I feel under the weather.

literal_meaning: An event happening when the moon turns blue
real_meaning: Very rarely or hardly ever
example: My family goes to luxury cinema screenings only once in a blue moon.

idiom: Cost an arm and a leg
literal_meaning: Pay by surrendering two limbs
real_meaning: To be extremely expensive
example: The front-row tickets to the concert cost an arm and a leg.

literal_meaning: Via the actual vines of grapes
real_meaning: Learned through informal rumors or gossip
example: I heard through the grapevine that our department is getting a new manager.

idiom: Take it with a grain of salt
literal_meaning: Eat food accompanied by a single grain of table salt
real_meaning: To regard something with skepticism or not accept it literally
example: You should take online reviews with a grain of salt.

literal_meaning: Possessing two complete physical planets
real_meaning: Enjoying the advantages of two different situations at once
example: Working remotely while living in the mountains offers the best of both worlds.

idiom: The ball is in your court
literal_meaning: A sports ball has landed on your side of the playing area
real_meaning: It is your turn or responsibility to make the next decision or step
example: I sent them our final proposal; now the ball is in their court.

literal_meaning: A dog barking at a tree where no prey is located
real_meaning: Pursuing a mistaken line of thought or asking the wrong person
example: If you think I broke the printer, you are barking up the wrong tree.

literal_meaning: Floating on cloud classification number nine
real_meaning: Extremely happy, joyful, or elated
example: When she received her grant acceptance letter, she was on cloud nine.

literal_meaning: Look directly into someone else's eye level
real_meaning: To agree fully with someone on a topic
example: My business partner and I don't always see eye to eye, but we respect each other.

literal_meaning: Hit the bushes with sticks to startle birds
real_meaning: To avoid talking about the main issue or point directly
example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what really happened.

literal_meaning: A sacred favor wearing a costume
real_meaning: An apparent misfortune that eventually results in something good
example: Missing that flight was a blessing in disguise because I met my future partner on the next one.

literal_meaning: Slice off the sharp corners of an object
real_meaning: To do something in the easiest or cheapest way, sacrificing quality
example: The builders cut corners when renovating the roof, and now it leaks.

literal_meaning: Physically punch a burlap bag
real_meaning: To go to sleep or go to bed
example: I have an early train tomorrow morning, so I am going to hit the sack.

literal_meaning: Tug or pull on a person's lower limb
real_meaning: To tease or joke with someone by telling them something untrue
example: Relax, I'm not really selling my car; I was just pulling your leg!

literal_meaning: Offering one cent to hear what someone is thinking
real_meaning: A friendly way of asking someone what they are thinking about when quiet
example: You've been staring out the window for ten minutes—a penny for your thoughts?

literal_meaning: Utter the name of the devil
real_meaning: Said when a person appears right after being mentioned in conversation
example: Speak of the devil! We were just talking about how great your presentation was.

literal_meaning: Verbally mock someone right after hurting them physically
real_meaning: To make a bad situation even worse with an additional offense
example: Our flight was delayed five hours, and to add insult to injury, our luggage was lost.

literal_meaning: Smash solid ice on water
real_meaning: To initiate conversation in a social setting to relieve tension
example: The host played a funny game to break the ice at the beginning of the workshop.

literal_meaning: Walk or drive one additional mile beyond your destination
real_meaning: To make a special effort beyond what is required
example: Our English teacher always goes the extra mile to help students understand tricky grammar.

idiom: Let the cat out of the bag
literal_meaning: Release a feline from a sack
real_meaning: To accidentally reveal a secret or hidden intention
example: Don't let the cat out of the bag about the surprise promotion until tomorrow.

literal_meaning: Fail to board a departing ferry or ship
real_meaning: To miss an opportunity by acting too late
example: If you don't apply for the study abroad program today, you might miss the boat.

literal_meaning: Perch physical body on a wooden fence
real_meaning: To remain neutral and delay making a decision between two options
example: You can't sit on the fence forever; you need to choose which project to join.
